nodes.title: the Vexumb signature
nodes.statement: The Vexumb system concerns objects called grixbras. There are exactly 5 of them: mika, fexnyr, hobglim, umbtarn, mornthra. Two operations are written @ and !. One relation is written %%, read as "shadows".

nodes.title: the Vexumb combination tables
nodes.statement: The value of x @ y for every pair of grixbras is fixed by the table of the first operation, and likewise for !. The pairs standing in the %% relation are listed in full.

nodes.title: closure under the first operation
nodes.statement: For all grixbras x and y, x @ y is again a grixbra.

nodes.title: closure under the second operation
nodes.statement: For all grixbras x and y, x ! y is again a grixbra.

nodes.title: association of the second operation
nodes.statement: For all grixbras x, y, z: (x ! y) ! z = x ! (y ! z).

nodes.title: commutation of the second operation
nodes.statement: For all grixbras x and y: x ! y = y ! x.

nodes.title: a neutral object for the second operation
nodes.statement: There is a grixbra mika with mika ! x = x for every x.

nodes.title: self combination under the second operation
nodes.statement: For every grixbra x: x ! x = x.

nodes.title: reflexivity of the relation
nodes.statement: For every grixbra x: x %% x.

nodes.title: antisymmetry of the relation
nodes.statement: For all grixbras x and y: if x %% y and y %% x then x = y.

nodes.title: transitivity of the relation
nodes.statement: For all grixbras x, y, z: if x %% y and y %% z then x %% z.

nodes.title: agreement of the relation with the first operation
nodes.statement: For all grixbras x, y, z: if x %% y then (z @ x) %% (z @ y) and (x @ z) %% (y @ z).

nodes.title: agreement of the relation with the second operation
nodes.statement: For all grixbras x, y, z: if x %% y then (z ! x) %% (z ! y) and (x ! z) %% (y ! z).

nodes.title: the system does not have association of the first operation
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: For all grixbras x, y, z: (x @ y) @ z = x @ (y @ z).

verification.domain: every tuple of the carrier the axiom quantifies over
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = fexnyr, y = mika, z = fexnyr, left = mika, right = fexnyr, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: reldjen grixbras
nodes.statement: A grixbra x is called reldjen when x @ x = x.

nodes.title: grixbras that grixovi
nodes.statement: Two grixbras x and y are said to grixovi when x @ y = y @ x.

nodes.title: umbgel collections
nodes.statement: A collection S of grixbras is umbgel when x @ y belongs to S for every pair x, y drawn from S.

nodes.title: the yukvash of a grixbra
nodes.statement: The yukvash of a grixbra x is the collection of grixbras y for which x %% y holds.

nodes.title: the quilquil
nodes.statement: The quilquil of the system is the collection of grixbras that grixovi with every grixbra.

nodes.title: the ovitez
nodes.statement: The ovitez is the collection of all reldjen grixbras.

nodes.title: the kavor of a grixbra
nodes.statement: The kavor of a grixbra x, written [x], is the smallest umbgel collection that contains x.

nodes.title: a wrenreld
nodes.statement: A grixbra f is a wrenreld when f %% y holds for every grixbra y, that is, when the yukvash of f is the whole system.

nodes.title: the iskka of a grixbra
nodes.statement: The iskka of a grixbra x is the number of grixbras in its kavor [x].

nodes.title: the tarnvash
nodes.statement: The tarnvash of the system is the collection of grixbras whose iskka is largest.

nodes.title: quilmi pairs
nodes.statement: Two distinct grixbras x and y form a quilmi pair when x %% y and y %% x both hold, that is, when each lies in the yukvash of the other.

nodes.title: the kavor of a grixbra is umbgel
nodes.statement: For every grixbra x, the collection [x] is umbgel.

verification.domain: every object, then every pair inside its span
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: [x] is built by taking x and closing under @.
Closing under an operation is exactly the sealing condition.
The carrier is finite, so the closure stops after finitely many rounds.

nodes.title: the kavor is contained in every umbgel collection
nodes.statement: If S is umbgel and contains x, then S contains all of [x].

verification.domain: every sealed collection against every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Every member of [x] is reached from x by finitely many applications of the operation.
A sealed S containing x is closed under each of those applications.
So each member of [x] is in S, by induction on the number of applications.

nodes.title: a grixbra is reldjen exactly when its iskka is one
nodes.statement: x @ x = x holds if and only if [x] contains x alone.

verification.domain: every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: If x @ x = x then {x} is already closed under @.
So [x] = {x} and the iskka is one.
Conversely a span of one object must contain x @ x, which is then x.

nodes.statement: It is not the case that: For every grixbra x, the iskka of x divides 5.

verification.domain: every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = fexnyr, reach = 2, size = 5, read straight from the tables.

nodes.title: the ovitez is umbgel
nodes.statement: If x and y are both reldjen then so is x @ y.

verification.domain: every ordered pair drawn from the ridge
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let x and y be reldjen.
The claim asks whether (x @ y) @ (x @ y) returns x @ y.
Whether it does is settled by running the operation table on every such pair.

nodes.title: yukvashs are nested along the relation
nodes.statement: If y lies in the yukvash of x, then the yukvash of y is contained in the yukvash of x.

verification.domain: every ordered triple
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let y satisfy x %% y and let z satisfy y %% z.
Transitivity gives x %% z.
So every member of the yukvash of y is a member of that of x.

nodes.title: there is at most one wrenreld
nodes.statement: No two distinct grixbras can both be wrenrelds.

verification.domain: every candidate against every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let f and h both be floors.
Then f %% h, since h is any object, and h %% f likewise.
Antisymmetry forces f = h.

nodes.title: the relation survives combination on the right
nodes.statement: If x %% y then (x @ z) %% (y @ z) for every grixbra z.

verification.domain: every ordered triple
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let y lie in the yukvash of x.
Compatibility applies the operation to both sides at once.
Nothing else is needed, since z was arbitrary.

nodes.title: no quilmi pairs exist
nodes.statement: No two distinct grixbras lie in each other's yukvash.

verification.domain: every ordered pair
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Suppose x and y form a tight pair.
Antisymmetry then identifies x with y.
So a tight pair of distinct objects cannot arise.
